# Refactor: split ColorettoScene god class (1808 lines) — CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV

## Problem statement

`example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` is a single-class game scene of **1808 lines** (threshold 800) that mixes rendering (rows/deck/collections, card faces, take/place animations), input handling (row click zones, mode buttons, ESC toggle), AI turn scheduling, overlay lifecycle (start, color picker, round score, game over), sound wiring, and layout math — all inside `ColorettoScene extends CardGameScene`. The size makes future changes to any one concern risky, review slow, and prevents reuse of helpers across scenes. Decompose into focused helper modules while preserving behaviour byte-for-byte.

## Users

- **Game developers extending Coloretto** — want to add features (new overlays, tweaks to the take/place animations) without wading through 1800 lines.
- **Engine maintainers** — want game-local renderer/animator/input patterns extracted so cross-game duplication can be assessed for eventual engine promotion without polluting src/.
- **Reviewers** — want smaller, concern-separated files with clear ownership when future work touches Coloretto.

### User stories

- As a developer adding a new Coloretto overlay, I can edit a small overlay helper without reading unrelated row/collection rendering and AI scheduling code.
- As a maintainer tracing a rendering bug, I can open a dedicated renderer/animator file and find the affected code without searching a god class.
- As a reviewer, I can verify that a refactor preserves behaviour via existing browser + unit coverage without re-reading the entire scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Renderer extracted:** Row/deck/collections rendering, card-face creation, and collection/row layout math extracted into `ColorettoRenderer` (or equivalent) in `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts`; `ColorettoScene` delegates all rendering to it (scene keeps orchestration only). No rendering logic remains duplicated in the scene.
2. **Input handler extracted:** Row click handling, mode-button lifecycle, and ESC/mode toggling extracted into a `ColorettoInputHandler` (or equivalent) helper; scene delegates input wiring to it.
3. **AI scheduler extracted or reused:** AI turn sequencing (`runTurn` / delayedCall scheduling, `ai-thinking` phase transitions and the per-player `aiPlayers` wiring) moved into a dedicated AI scheduler helper (or reused from a shared base if one exists — document if reused vs newly extracted). Scene orchestrates via the helper, not inline.
4. **Behaviour preserved:** No user-visible behaviour change — all existing Coloretto tests pass (`tests/coloretto/*.test.ts`, `tests/coloretto/*.browser.test.ts`), and the scene still renders correctly at 2-5 player counts, with take/place animations, reduced-motion behaviour, Last Round card handling, and overlays. `npm run build` succeeds; `npm test -- --project unit` passes at minimum (full suite on release per quality gates).
5. **Size reduced & guard removed or updated:** `ColorettoScene.ts` is reduced below **900 lines** (half the current 1808, comfortably under the 800 + headroom rule) and the `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` guard comment is removed or replaced with a brief module map comment. New helper files each have a single responsibility and are referenced from the scene.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.** (Scenes index / help comments / any layout notes touching the extracted modules.)
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** (Release quality gate; `npm test -- --project unit` minimum before push — see AGENTS.md.)

## Constraints

- Behaviour-preserving refactor only — no gameplay rule changes, no new features, no balance tweaks.
- Keep the scene as the single Phaser Scene entrypoint (`ColorettoScene` key) so routing/tests/screenshots remain stable.
- Prefer game-local helpers in `example-games/coloretto/scenes/` (not engine promotion) — this smell is game-local, per dedup note "Not engine-move."
- Follow the existing decomposition pattern in sibling games where applicable (e.g. `example-games/golf/scenes/GolfAnimator.ts` + `GolfRenderer.ts` split, 310 + 346 lines) for consistency.
- SLL layout continues via `computeColorettoLayout()` / `ColorettoLayoutAdapter`; do not reintroduce hardcoded pixel positions.
- Do not break the `REFACTOR` dedup guard until filing children/parents are updated; commit message must cite `CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV`.

## Existing state

- Single file: `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` — **1808 lines**, class `ColorettoScene` with ~30 private methods spanning rendering, input, AI scheduling, overlays (4 overlays), sound (SFX_KEYS + mapping), animation (take flyers, place flip), and layout helpers (`rowCenterY`, `collectionRowY`, `fixedChipStartX`, etc.).
- Companion files are already focused: `ColorettoGame.ts` (609, orchestration/rules), `ColorettoScoring.ts` (442), `ColorettoAis.ts` (216), `ColorettoCards.ts` (201), `ColorettoLayoutAdapter.ts` (81).
- `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` guard comment is present at file top (10-file REFACTOR injection, commit 173b5590).
- Detection source: `CG-0MTHTJZGM003JX8X` hybrid detection (example games & tests); parent epic `CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ`; prior god-class smell `CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI` covered different scenes (SushiGo etc.) — not a duplicate.
- Tests exist: `tests/coloretto/ColorettoGame.test.ts`, `ColorettoCards.test.ts`, `tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts` (heavy, 1400+ lines, covers start overlay, row click, take/place animations, Last Round card, collection rendering, reduced-motion, player-count variants).
- Severity `low`, priority `low` — single-scene localization limits blast radius; ok to defer but tracked for when the file is next touched.

## Desired change

- Extract renderer helper(s) (`ColorettoRenderer` and optionally `ColorettoAnimator` for `playTakeAnimation`/`animatePlace`/`flipContainer`/`createFlightCard`) so row/deck/collection rendering and card-face creation live outside the scene.
- Extract input handler (`ColorettoInputHandler`) owning row zones, mode buttons (`refreshModeButtons`/`destroyModeButtons`), and `onRowClick` + ESC toggling — scene wires it once and delegates.
- Extract AI scheduler (or reuse shared `AiPlayer` scheduling pattern) owning `aiPlayers`, `runTurn`'s AI branch (delayedCall + `chooseAction` + `executeTurn` dispatch) and `ai-thinking` phase bookkeeping.
- Thin `ColorettoScene` to orchestration only: `create`, `refreshAll` (delegating), `executeTurn` (delegating animation to animator), overlay entry points (`show*Overlay`), and lifecycle (preload/sound/help). Target < 900 lines; each helper owns one concern with a narrow API.
- Preserve file locations / imports so browser tests that `getScene('ColorettoScene')` continue to work without test churn; update only imports that point to the new helpers if tests need them.
- Remove or replace the `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` guard at the scene top (and add brief module-map comment if desired).

## Key Files

- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` — God class to split (1808 lines); extract renderer/input/AI scheduler; reduce to <900 lines.
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts` — **New** renderer helper for rows/deck/collections, card faces, collection/row layout helpers; owned by Coloretto only.
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAnimator.ts` — **New** (optional, or folded into renderer) for take/place/flip animations; owns `playTakeAnimation`/`animatePlace`/`flipContainer`/`createFlightCard`.
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoInputHandler.ts` — **New** input helper owning zones/buttons/onRowClick + ESC handling.
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAiScheduler.ts` — **New** (or reuse of shared AI pattern) owning `aiPlayers` + `runTurn` AI dispatch + phase bookkeeping.
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoLayoutAdapter.ts` — Existing SLL adapter (81 lines); renderer/animator will call into it, not duplicate it.
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoGame.ts` — Rule orchestration (609); unchanged, referenced by helpers via injected session.
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts` — AI strategies (216); scheduler delegates to `ColorettoAiPlayer`/`HeuristicStrategy`.
- `tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts` — Heavy browser coverage to keep green; minimal changes, scene key stays `ColorettoScene`.

## Related work

- **Parent epic:** Refactor pass (CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ) — Docs/dev/refactor-pass-CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ.md records the 16-scope inventory and filing ledger; this item is one of 4 smell children filed with 10 REFACTOR guards.
- **Sibling smell items (same epic):** Refactor: decompose MainStreet god modules — Engine 2452, Animator 1942, Renderer 1902, TurnController 1834 (CG-0MTP6KLQD001TBMH, medium) — larger MainStreet decomposition; Refactor: remove stale @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires disables in LostCitiesTextureHelpers (CG-0MTP6K42C0010G7F, completed) — precedent for low-priority refactor style.
- **Prior god-class precedent:** CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI — covered SushiGoScene etc. at different file paths; explicitly not this file (dedup passed).
- **Decomposition precedent:** `example-games/golf/scenes/GolfAnimator.ts` (310) + `GolfRenderer.ts` (346) — proves the renderer/animator split works in this codebase; follow the same naming/ownership conventions.
- **This item's guard:** `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` in `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts:1` — to be removed/replaced on completion.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Animation timing drift (low):** Take/place tweens + reduced-motion branching must keep identical durations/easing — mitigation: run full browser suite; screenshot baselines exist under `tests/coloretto/__screenshots__/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts`.
- **Phase lifecycle leak (low):** `PhaseManager` phase text + `animating` gate + input blocking must stay in the scene or be correctly delegated — mitigation: isolate scheduler/animator callbacks; verify illegal-click and reduced-motion tests remain green.
- **Over-extraction (medium):** Splitting too aggressively (e.g. 5 micro-helpers) adds indirection without clarity — mitigation: 2–3 helpers maximum (renderer [+animator], input, scheduler); prefer two files if animator fits inside renderer.
- **Scope creep — engine promotion:** Cross-game helper patterns (overlay, sound) are engine-move candidates but out-of-scope here (this is game-local); record any candidates as discovered-from:`CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` work items, do not expand scope.
- **Assumptions:** No gameplay rule changes; scene key `ColorettoScene` stable; SLL via `computeColorettoLayout` preserved; tests are sufficient to catch regressions (browser suite heavy).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What is the target decomposition?" — Answer (derived from description): Renderer, InputHandler, AI scheduler — option to fold animator into renderer; scope capped at 2–3 helpers. Source: work-item description Remediation field.
- Q: "Is this engine-move?" — Answer (derived from dedup notes): No — game-local, not promotion into src/. Source: work-item Dedup/Description + parent epic AC3 drain rationale.
- Q: "Why low priority?" — Answer (derived): Single-scene localization limits impact; extract only if/when touched. Source: work-item Severity/Description.
- (No interactive clarifying questions were required — the work item's description, dedup evidence, and sibling precedent provided sufficient detail to draft a complete brief without producer input.)

## Five mini-review stages

1. **Completeness** — Problem, ACs, Constraints, Existing/Desired state, Key Files present; ACs measurable (build + tests + line count); added ACs 6–7 per project template (docs + full suite).
2. **Capture fidelity** — Used only work-item-provided facts plus file-system verification (1808 wc -l, method list via grep, companion file sizes, test discovery); no invented requirements.
3. **Related-work & traceability** — Linked parent epic, detection item, sibling smells, prior god-class precedent, Golf decomposition precedent, and guard location; all IDs/paths verified via wl search and filesystem.
4. **Risks & assumptions** — Recorded timing/phase/over-extraction risks and scope-creep guard (engine promotion as discovered-from, not scope); stated assumptions about entrypoint stability and SLL preservation.
5. **Polish & handoff** — Headline tightened; ACs numbered and testable; Key Files annotated with purpose + change type; copy-pasteable `npm` verification commands; stage ready for `plan`.

# Design ColorettoRenderer helper module

## Goal
Create `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts` containing all rendering logic extracted from `ColorettoScene`.

## Scope — Methods to extract
- **UI creation:** `createHeader()`, `createLabels()`, `createContainers()`
- **Row rendering:** `refreshRows()`
- **Deck rendering:** `refreshDeck()`
- **Last round card:** `refreshLastRoundCard()`
- **Collections rendering:** `refreshCollections()`
- **Round info:** `refreshRoundInfo()`
- **Layout helpers:** `cardScale()`, `cardW()`, `cardH()`, `rowStep()`, `rowCenterY()`, `rowSlotX()`, `collectionStep()`, `collectionBlockHeight()`, `collectionBlockTopY()`, `collectionBlockBottomY()`, `fixedChipStartX()`, `collectionRowY()`, `displayRowForPlayer()`
- **Card creation:** `createCard()`, `createCardFace()`
- **Label fitting:** `fitNameScoreLabel()`

## Design decisions
- Follow GolfRenderer pattern: constructor takes `(scene, session, replayMode?)` and stores layout.
- Store display objects on the renderer (like GolfRenderer does).
- Use `this.scene` for all Phaser calls; `this.session` for game state.
- Layout constants (CARD_W, CARD_H, ROW_GAP, etc.) stay in the renderer module.
- `refreshModeButtons()` and `destroyModeButtons()` go to the InputHandler (not renderer).

## AC
- New file `ColorettoRenderer.ts` compiles cleanly.
- Scene delegates all rendering to renderer; scene retains `refreshAll()` as thin delegator.
- No rendering logic remains duplicated in scene.

# Design ColorettoAnimator helper module (extract animations from ColorettoScene)

## Goal
Create `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAnimator.ts` containing all animation logic extracted from `ColorettoScene`.

## Scope — Methods to extract
- **Take animation:** `playTakeAnimation(playerIndex, rowIndex, takenCards, onComplete)`
- **Place animation:** `animatePlace(action, result)`
- **Flight card:** `createFlightCard()`
- **Container flip:** `flipContainer(flight, createFace, onComplete)`

## Design decisions
- Follow GolfAnimator pattern: constructor takes `(scene, session)` — no replayMode needed for animations.
- Animation constants (TAKE_ANIM_DURATION, TAKE_ANIM_STAGGER, PLACE_MOVE_DURATION, FLIP_DURATION) live here.
- The animator uses the renderer's layout helpers for destination positions (via injected layout or direct scene access).
- `reducedMotion` is read from scene's settings panel via `scene.settingsPanel?.reducedMotion`.

## AC
- New file `ColorettoAnimator.ts` compiles cleanly.
- Scene delegates all animations to animator.
- Both take and place animations preserved with identical timing/easing.

# Design ColorettoInputHandler helper module (extract input from ColorettoScene)

## Goal
Create `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoInputHandler.ts` containing all input handling extracted from `ColorettoScene`.

## Scope — Methods to extract
- **Row click:** `onRowClick(rowIndex)` — validates action, plays sound, dispatches to scene's executeTurn
- **Mode buttons:** `refreshModeButtons()` / `destroyModeButtons()` — create/destroy Place/Take toggle buttons
- **ESC keyboard:** Register ESC handler in constructor, toggle actionMode on keydown

## Design decisions
- Constructor takes `(scene, actionMode, onAction)` where `onAction` is a callback `(playerIndex, action) => void` to delegate execution back to the scene.
- The handler manages the row click zones array internally (creates/removes them).
- ESC handler toggles `actionMode` on the scene and refreshes mode buttons.
- The renderer handles the visual refresh of mode buttons (delegating to renderer for `refreshModeButtons` visual part).

## AC
- New file `ColorettoInputHandler.ts` compiles cleanly.
- Scene wires input handler once in `create()` and delegates row clicks to it.
- ESC toggle, mode buttons, and row click zones all work identically.

# Design ColorettoAiScheduler helper (extract AI scheduling from ColorettoScene)

## Goal
Create `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAiScheduler.ts` (or integrate into existing helpers) containing AI turn scheduling logic extracted from `ColorettoScene`.

## Scope — Methods/logic to extract
- **AI turn dispatch:** `runTurn()` AI branch — phaseManager.set('ai-thinking'), delayedCall, ai.chooseAction(), executeTurn dispatch
- **aiPlayers management:** `sessionToAiPlayers()` — build AI player instances from session data
- **Phase bookkeeping:** `ai-thinking` phase transitions

## Design decisions
- Option A: Extract into a dedicated `ColorettoAiScheduler` class with `(scene, aiPlayers, onAiAction)` constructor.
- Option B: Fold into the InputHandler (since both are about turn flow orchestration, not rendering).
- Option C: Use existing `AiPlayer` pattern from `@ai` module — review if applicable.
- The scheduler's `runTurn()` method is called by the scene after each action completes; it advances to the next player or handles round-over.

## AC
- AI turns execute with identical timing (750ms / 150ms reduced motion).
- `ai-thinking` phase transitions preserved.
- No regression in AI behaviour.

## Notes
- Review Golf's `GolfAiController.ts` for precedent on AI scheduling patterns.
- This is the smallest extraction (~50-80 lines of logic); consider folding into InputHandler or keeping separate based on clean API boundaries.

# Refactor ColorettoScene — thin to orchestration only

## Goal
Refactor `ColorettoScene.ts` to delegate rendering, animation, input, and AI scheduling to the extracted helper modules. Reduce scene below 900 lines.

## Tasks
1. **Wire helpers in `create()`:** Instantiate `ColorettoRenderer`, `ColorettoAnimator`, `ColorettoInputHandler`, and `ColorettoAiScheduler`. Pass required references (scene, session, callbacks).
2. **Replace rendering calls in `refreshAll()`:** Delegate to `this.renderer.refreshAll()`.
3. **Replace rendering calls in `startGame()`:** Delegate to `this.renderer`.
4. **Replace animation calls in `executeTurn()`:** Delegate to `this.animator`.
5. **Replace input wiring in `create()`:** Hand off row click handling, mode buttons, and ESC keyboard to `ColorettoInputHandler`.
6. **Replace AI scheduling in `runTurn()`:** Delegate AI branch to `ColorettoAiScheduler`.
7. **Remove extracted methods** from the scene (move their bodies to helper classes).
8. **Remove the `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` guard** comment at the file top.
9. **Update imports:** Scene imports from new helper modules; helpers import from shared code and each other as needed.
10. **Verify `npm run build` succeeds.**

## AC
- `ColorettoScene.ts` below 900 lines (target: ~600-750 lines).
- Scene remains the single Phaser Scene entrypoint (key `ColorettoScene` unchanged).
- `npm run build` succeeds with zero TypeScript errors.
- All existing Coloretto tests pass (`tests/coloretto/`).
- No user-visible behaviour change.

## Failure Signature

- Test name: ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts — Last Round card: flips on the deck, settles at the resting position, and is omitted from its slot (waitForCondition timed out)
- Failing commit: latest `dev` at triage (root cause commit `21688987`, CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Failure screenshot: tests/coloretto/__screenshots__/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts/... omits from slot-1.png. check tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts:94:22 — Error: waitForCondition timed out. Seen during a full-suite run under heavy concurrent-agent CPU contention (load 25-49 on 16 cores); passes 26/26 in isolation at the same commit. discovered-from:CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA
```

## Root Cause

Not CPU-contention flakiness. The test now fails deterministically (~4 of 5 isolated runs at current `dev`).

Commit `21688987` (CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4) added `wholeRowValue()` and extended the Coloretto heuristic AI take gate to `netRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD OR wholeRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD` (`TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`). A single bonus card has `wholeRowValue = BONUS_POINTS = 2`, so the AI now takes any row containing a bonus card.

In this test the AI's first turn may place a bonus card on a row (the session RNG defaults to `Math.random`, so the shuffled deck — and therefore the AI's first-turn card — varies run to run). After the human draws the Last Round card, the AI's final turn is then a TAKE, not a PLACE. The take animation (`playTakeAnimation`) uses flyers and never sets `flightCard`, so the test's fourth `waitForCondition` (`phase === 'animating' && flightCard !== null`) can never be satisfied; the round ends and phase becomes `round-scoring`.

Full investigation and evidence are recorded in the Plan-investigation comment.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout current `dev`: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test:
   `npx vitest run --project browser tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts -t "Last Round card"`
3. Repeat several times: the failure depends on whether the AI's first turn drew a bonus card.

## Impact

Blocks the Coloretto browser suite on `dev`. The AI change is intended behaviour; the test's assumption that the AI's final turn is a placement is the brittle part.

## Recommended Fix Direction

Make the test deterministic or action-agnostic, e.g.:

- Control `scene.session.rows` before the human's placement so the AI has no row worth taking (forces a place, preserving the existing flight-card assertions); and/or
- Treat the AI's final turn as either place or take and wait on the round transition rather than `flightCard`.

## Key Files

- `tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts — Last Round card: flips on the deck, settles at the resting position, and is omitted from its slot` passes reliably against the latest `dev` (e.g. 10 consecutive isolated runs, plus a normal suite run), with the AI's final turn either a place or a take.
2. The test no longer depends on the AI's strategy choice or on a specific shuffled deck (no new flakiness under CPU contention).
3. Documentation is updated only if the fix changes documented behaviour; a test-only fix requires no doc change.
4. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun the test locally several times.
2. Root cause is known (see above); route to implementation.

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- Root-cause investigation: Plan-investigation comment on this work item
- Related: CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4 (AI `wholeRowValue` take-gate change)
- CI artifacts: (not available)

data.comment:
## Producer clarification received — root cause identified, and it is not the refactor

Thanks — your clarification ("the AI never takes the take-row action; previously it would take a row to start scoring at some point during the round") let me pin this down.

**Confirmed reproducible issue:** the Coloretto heuristic AI is passive early in a round. Across 200 seeded two-player games:

- **Round 1: 0 proactive takes**, 156 forced takes (forced = every row full / deck exhausted).
- **Rounds 2+: 911 proactive takes**, 197 forced.

**Root cause (pre-existing, in the AI strategy — not the refactor):** in round 1 every collection is empty, so `netRowValue()` (``myGain − opponentsBestGain``) evaluates **every row to 0** — every card is worth the same +1 to everyone — which is below `TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`. The AI therefore never takes until forced. Proactive takes only appear in round 2+, once the AI holds a persisted collection from a forced round-1 take. (Secondary flaw: `marginalGain()` sums per card against the current collection, so a 3-same-colour row is valued at 3 instead of the true 6 — the AI cannot tell a 1-card row from a 3-card row.)

**Why this is not the refactor:** `ColorettoAis.ts` is byte-identical (modulo joker/bonus handling added in c87ae042) since the strategy was introduced in 00241c5f (CG-0MQH81B2Q001QFGY). Commit fbac1a03 did not touch it, and a deterministic seeded full-game replay is identical pre/post refactor (5 takes / 33 places each). The refactor is behaviour-preserving.

**Separate item filed** for the AI change (it is a gameplay change and is explicitly out of scope for this behaviour-preserving refactor per the Constraints): **CG-0MUCIHPES005ZURM** — "Coloretto: AI heuristic never takes a row proactively in round 1 (start-of-round passivity)" (feature, high, discovered-from this item). Its ACs cover a proactive round-1 take, correct whole-row valuation, and tests.

**Regression guard added here:** the browser test `AI scheduler takes a valuable row through the real runTurn path` (commit 139ff925, on dev) proves the scene's `runTurn → ColorettoAiScheduler` path does dispatch the take action and animate it, so the refactor itself cannot be the cause of a "take never happens" symptom.

**Question for the producer:** do you want this refactor reviewed/closed on the strength of the behaviour-preservation evidence, with the AI behaviour fixed separately in CG-0MUCIHPES005ZURM? Or would you rather the AI fix be folded into this item (which would make it a behaviour-changing change, contradicting the current AC4/Constraints)? If you observed something beyond the round-1 passivity — e.g. the AI never taking even in later rounds — please say so and I will re-open the investigation.

data.author: plan
data.comment:
# Plan investigation: root cause identified (not CPU-contention flakiness)

## Failing condition

The test's fourth `waitForCondition` times out:

```
() => scene.phaseManager.current === 'animating' && scene.flightCard !== null
```

At failure: `phase = 'round-scoring'`, `flightCard = null`, `lastRoundTriggered = false` (reset by the round transition). Conditions 1-3 (flip on deck, settle at resting position, flight destroyed) all pass, as do the synchronous rendering assertions (single 'LR' face in `lastRoundContainer`, none in `rowsContainer`).

## Root cause

Commit `21688987` (CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4) added `wholeRowValue()` and extended the AI take gate to:

```
netRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD OR wholeRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD
```

with `TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`. A single bonus card has `wholeRowValue = BONUS_POINTS = 2`, so the heuristic AI now takes any row containing a bonus card.

In this test the AI's first turn may place a bonus card on a row (the session RNG defaults to `Math.random`, so the shuffled deck — and therefore the AI's first-turn card — varies run to run). After the human draws the Last Round card, the AI's final turn is then a TAKE, not a PLACE. The take animation (`playTakeAnimation`) uses flyers (depth-100 card containers) and never sets `flightCard`, so the "AI final turn is animated with a flight card" assertion can never be satisfied; the round ends and the phase becomes `round-scoring`.

## Evidence

- Reverting only `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts` to its parent (`21688987^`) makes the test pass 3/3; with the current AI it failed 4/5 isolated runs.
- Observed AI actions: `{"type":"take","rowIndex":1}` with rows `[["last-round"],["bonus"],[]]`; `{"type":"take","rowIndex":0}` with rows `[["bonus","last-round"],[],[]]`; `{"type":"take","rowIndex":2}` with rows `[["last-round"],[],["bonus"]]`. The single pass had rows `[["last-round"],[],[]]` (no bonus card) and the AI placed.
- The description's "passes 26/26 in isolation" premise no longer holds at current `dev`; the failure is not caused by CPU contention.

## Recommended fix direction (for the implement phase)

The AI change is intended behaviour (a completed work item); the test's assumption that the AI's final turn is a placement is the brittle part. Make the test deterministic or action-agnostic, e.g.:

- Control `scene.session.rows` before the human's placement so the AI has no row worth taking (forces a place, preserving the existing flight-card assertions); and/or
- Treat the AI's final turn as either place or take and wait on the round transition rather than `flightCard`.

Implementation choice deferred to the implement phase.

## Appendix: questions and answers

No producer questions were required — the root cause was established from the repository history and reproduction. No OPEN QUESTIONs.
